issues.detail: Covers the happy path but gives no guidance on handling failures such as missing columns, empty DataFrames, connection errors, or how to read failed results and partial failures (e.g. unexpected_index_list, mostly).

The SQL connection string contains a literal ${WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD} that Python will not expand, the severity guideline gives no code, and the Data Docs generation mentioned in the description is never shown.
Example 2 reuses an undefined checkpoint from earlier and shows no expectation or suite for the status set, and neither example shows a failing result or output.

scenarios.name: validate-csv-before-warehouse-load
scenarios.rationale: Both responses match the rubric's GX 1.x in-code flow and class-object expectations and end with batch.validate(suite), so they are nearly identical on coverage; A adds more notes on edge cases but B is equally correct and uses the explicit gx.expectations path.

scenarios.name: postgres-checkpoint-gate-for-airflow
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric item, including the Checkpoint via context.checkpoints.add and raising when checkpoint_result.success is false. B omits the Checkpoint and calls ValidationDefinition.run() directly, so it misses the required checkpoints.add wiring, though its other pieces are solid.

scenarios.name: migrate-old-gx-tutorial-code
scenarios.rationale: Both identify the 0.18 vs 1.x API mismatch and give the right replacements; B matches the rubric more directly by showing the expectation added to an ExpectationSuite and `gx.get_context()` for init, while A's main example validates the expectation ad hoc (suite only in the second block) and uses `get_context(mode="file")`, a small deviation from the rubric's `gx.get_context()`.
